sheets.title: High Grade Emissions (HGE)
sheets.summary: The go-to source for rare grade-4/5 manufactured mats. You don't filter for HGE directly — you filter for the right kind of system, then honk.
sheets.what: HGE are a **Unidentified Signal Source** (usually **Threat 0**) that appear in supercruise. Which material is inside is decided by the **controlling faction's allegiance/economy** and its current **faction state** (Boom, War/Civil War, Civil Unrest, Outbreak). They spawn most reliably in **high-population systems (1M+)**.
find: Open the **Galaxy Map → Info** panel and hunt a **high-population** system (1,000,000+) whose controlling faction matches the allegiance/economy you need (see the table).
Check that system's **Factions** tab for the required **state** (Boom / War / Civil War / Civil Unrest / Outbreak). No state needed for the Empire/Federation ones.
Jump in, then **honk the FSS** or just fly toward the populated bodies — HGE show up as USS contacts.
Fly to the USS until it resolves to **"High Grade Emissions"**, throttle into the **blue drop zone**, and scoop the material canisters.
**Relog** (Menu → Resume) to respawn the HGE in a known-good system and repeat.
sheets.filter: Galaxy Map → high-population system + matching allegiance/economy + required faction state → honk FSS → drop into the HGE USS
tips: **Easiest G5 in the game: Imperial Shielding** — any high-pop Imperial system, no state needed. Load ~100, then trade down 6:1... actually **manufactured trades 6:1 down / 3:1 up** at a Manufactured Material Trader to fill any other category.
The **Boom** pool holds three proto-materials at once, so farming Proto Radiolic directly is slow — most people farm Imperial Shielding and **trade for** the protos.
**War/Civil War** and **Outbreak** states are rarer to find, so those mats are usually traded for rather than farmed.
Community trackers list recent HGE sightings from live player data — handy for finding an active spot fast.

sheets.title: Crystalline Shards — grade-4 raw mats
sheets.summary: The fastest way to fill grade-4 raw bins without a trader. One qualifying body reliably hands you one of the 7 rare raws in bulk.
sheets.what: Fields of tall crystal clusters on **airless volcanic worlds**. Shoot the clusters with the SRV and scoop the drops — each qualifying body gives **one grade-4 raw** (plus lower grades). The material is set by the **body's surface composition**, not the shard colour, so identify sites by **body**, not by colour.
find: Look for a landable body that is **airless (no atmosphere)**, has **volcanism**, and sits **≥ 12,000 Ls** from the system's main star (that distance is what keeps it cold enough).
The main star should be spectral type **A, F, G, K, M or S**.
On arrival run the **FSS**, then **DSS-probe** the body. Shard fields show up under the **BIOLOGICAL** heat-map filter (not Geological) — fumaroles are usually co-located.
DSS-mapping drops nav waypoints straight to the fields. Drop in, board the **SRV**, shoot the **Crystalline Clusters**, scoop the mats.
Fill to the **100 cap**, then trade down 1→3 at a **Raw Material Trader** to fill the rest of that category's column.
sheets.filter: System map → airless + volcanic body, >12,000 Ls from an A/F/G/K/M/S star → DSS probe → BIOLOGICAL heat-map filter → SRV the clusters
tips: **HIP 36601 is the famous one-stop system** — four shard bodies covering Polonium, Ruthenium, Tellurium and Technetium. **Outotz LS-K d8-3** adds Yttrium and Antimony. Those two systems cover **6 of the 7** rare raws.
**Selenium is the odd one out** — it's rarely at shard sites; farm it from **Brain Trees** instead (see the Brain Trees card).
Closest shard cluster to the bubble is ~1,500 ly out in the **Sanguineous Rim** region — this is a deep-space trip, so bring the fuel-scoop build.
All 7 rare raws are **grade 4**, one at the top of each raw category — fill grade 4 and trade down to fill entire columns.

sheets.title: Brain Trees — Selenium & rare raws
sheets.summary: The main source for Selenium (which shards rarely give) and an alternative for grade-4 raws.
sheets.what: Organic tree-like structures whose **growth nodes**, when shot with the SRV and scooped, drop raw mats. The rarest node — **Phloem Excretion** — gives **grade-4** raws and grows on the 'brain' portion rather than the branches.
find: Find a **volcanic landable body** with **Guardian Ruins / ejecta craters** (recognisable from orbit by radiating lines), surface temp roughly **200–496 K**.
**DSS-map** the body and drop into a crater field. From above ~3 km, nodes show as tiny **blue POI blips** on radar.
Drive the SRV between the trees and shoot the node type you want — **Phloem Excretion** for grade 4 — then scoop.
tips: Known **Selenium** brain-tree sites: **Kappa-1 Volantis B 3 F A** and **HR 3230 3 A A**.
Each node gives ~1 unit vs ~3 per shard cluster, so use **shards** where available and brain trees mainly for **Selenium**.

sheets.title: Surface Prospecting — target a specific raw
sheets.summary: Every landable body has a fixed material menu. Pick a body rich in the raw you need and shoot the right rock type.
sheets.what: Drive the SRV over any landable body and shoot surface **mineral nodes**, then scoop (**×3 units** per drop). Each body's **Materials** list (system map) shows its fixed spread — typically **1 rare (G4), 2 standard (G3), 3 common (G2), 5 very-common (G1)** — so target a body whose G4 is the raw you want.
find: In the system map, read a body's **Materials** percentages and pick one rich in your target raw.
Land, deploy the SRV, and drive to **rocky deposits / volcanic protrusions**.
Shoot the node type that biases toward the grade you want (see table), then scoop.

yields.Grade bias: Random spread of the body's mats

tips: Drop rates are far lower than shard/brain-tree sites — prospecting is best for **topping up a specific mid-grade raw** a body is rich in, not bulk G4 farming.
Scan formations with the **Composition Scanner** for free Codex credit while you're there.

sheets.title: Geysers & Fumaroles — common raws
sheets.summary: Geological vents for near-universal common raws like Sulphur. Good for filling the bottom of a category.
sheets.what: Surface vents that emit gas and minerals. They spawn **geological POIs** with deposit nodes you harvest for common raws — the exact set depends on the vent/magma type and body composition.
find: Filter the **DSS heat-map to GEOLOGICAL** signals to find geyser/fumarole sites — this drops waypoints.
Drop in with the SRV; at each formation shoot the **Cobble/deposit** objects and scoop (×3 per drop).
tips: Best for **common raws** (Sulphur is near-universal), not grade-4 farming. Fumaroles often sit next to crystalline-shard fields, so you can do both in one landing.

sheets.title: Jameson Crash Site — encoded data goldmine
sheets.summary: The single best spot to farm high-grade encoded data. One SRV, a relog loop, and you fill up fast.
sheets.what: A crashed Cobra at **HIP 12099, body 1 B**. Sweeping the SRV turret over its data points yields **Adaptive Encryptors Capture (G5)** and **Atypical Encryption Archives (G4)** — the two 'currency' encryption mats you trade for anything else.
find: Jump to **HIP 12099**, supercruise to **planet 1**, drop to its moon **1 B**.
**DSS-probe** the body — the wreck POI is marked. Land near it and deploy the **SRV**.
Sit still and sweep the SRV **turret** across the blinking data points (≈9 of them).
When you get **"storage full / unable to receive data"**, Menu → **Resume** (mode relog) to respawn the points, then rescan.
Take the two encryption files to the **Encoded Material Trader** (nearest: **Ray Gateway, Diaguandri**) and trade for whatever encoded mats you actually need.
tips: This is faster than wake-scanning for **Datamined Wake Exceptions** — farm Adaptive Encryptors here and **trade up** for them (~2× faster).
No weapons needed; the site has no threats. Just an SRV and patience.

sheets.title: FSD Wake Scanning
sheets.summary: Encoded 'wake' data for FSD engineering — scan the clouds ships leave when they jump.
sheets.what: Fit a **Frame Shift Wake Scanner** (utility). Scan the **high wakes** (bright blue clouds left when a ship jumps to hyperspace) to collect **Datamined Wake Exceptions (G5)**, **Eccentric Hyperspace Trajectories (G4)**, **Strange Wake Solutions (G3)**, and lower.
find: Mount a **Frame Shift Wake Scanner** and head to a **busy Nav Beacon** or station no-fire zone in a **high-population** system.
Target the **High Wake** cloud a ship leaves as it hyperspace-jumps (not the low wakes from in-system travel).
Fly into scan range and let the scanner complete — the data drops straight into your Encoded storage.
tips: High-traffic hubs give the most wakes. If you only need Datamined Wake Exceptions, farm **Jameson** instead and trade up — it's faster.
The wake scanner also passively logs data while you fly — great to leave fitted on the Corsair mat build.

sheets.title: Settlement / Installation Data Points
sheets.summary: Rare firmware from scanning terminals at surface settlements, installations and megaships.
sheets.what: Fit a **Data Link Scanner** (utility) and scan the glowing **data terminals / comms arrays** at planetary settlements, surface POIs, installations and megaships. Source of rare firmware like **Modified Embedded Firmware (G5)** and **Specialised Legacy Firmware (G5)**.
find: Fit a **Data Link Scanner** utility module.
Drop at a **planetary settlement**, **installation** or **megaship** and target the glowing data comms points.
Hold the scan until complete. Small/abandoned and mission-target settlements often carry the rarest firmware.
tips: The very rarest G5 firmware is usually easier to get by farming Jameson data and **trading**, but data points are the direct in-world source.

sheets.title: Guardian Structures — module/weapon mats
sheets.summary: Shoot Sentinels with the SRV to farm the mats that unlock Guardian FSD boosters, hull, and weapons.
sheets.what: At a **Guardian Structure** you activate the central pylon, **Sentinels** spawn, and shooting them with the SRV drops **Guardian Power Cells, Power Conduits, Tech Components, Wreckage Components** and **Sentinel Wafers** — the mats a **Guardian Tech Broker** wants.
find: Fly to a **Guardian Structure** system (use the Guardian tab's finder), land near the site and deploy the **SRV** (bring spares — Sentinels destroy SRVs).
Drive to the **central structure** and activate it to spawn Sentinels.
**Shoot the Sentinels** with the SRV turret to collect their mats; scan the **pylons/relay** for Guardian data.
Grab the **Ancient Relic/Casket/Tablet/Totem/Urn** commodities if you need to activate obelisks.
tips: The **Corsair mat build** carries a size-6 SRV hangar for exactly this — redeploy without flying home.
You don't need ship weapons; the SRV does all the fighting.

sheets.title: Material Traders — turn junk into what you need
sheets.summary: The multiplier that makes all farming worth it. Farm one abundant mat, trade for the rest.
sheets.what: Three trader types (**Raw, Manufactured, Encoded**) let you convert materials **within a category**. You lose value on the exchange, but it means you never have to farm a specific rare mat — just farm an abundant one and trade.
tips: **Raw:** farm one common raw (e.g. from an abundant surface deposit or crystalline shards) and trade across the whole 7×4 grid.
**Manufactured:** farm **Imperial Shielding** at HGE, trade for anything.
**Encoded:** farm **Jameson** encryption data, trade for anything.
Trader **type** follows the station's economy — EliteOps' Materials tab finds the nearest of each type for you.
